extracted.intended_audience: authors, researchers, institutional press officers, and journalists interacting with Nature Portfolio journals (specifically Nature Methods)
extracted.subtask_short: press and embargo policy for journal articles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules governing how authors, institutions, and journalists may communicate about submitted, accepted, preprint, and in-press articles for Nature Portfolio journals, including embargo timing, press-release distribution, and preprint handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author solicitation of media discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid directly seeking media coverage for submitted manuscripts; premature solicitation is discouraged because it can pre-empt informed reporting and undermine peer review confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for author discussion with media (accepted contributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may speak to media about accepted papers only after the publication date is set and, where applicable, within the one-week window preceding publication, observing the stated embargo time and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release distribution and journalist access
rubrics_metrics.description: We produce and distribute press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists. Journalists receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website, together with other relevant material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release. Journalists are encouraged to read the full paper and are given corresponding authors' names and contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial highlighting of especially newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may add summaries to draw attention to notable papers; authors may receive media contact during this period and are encouraged to cooperate so coverage is accurate and balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors arranging their own publicity must adhere to embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may also arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors or their institutions publicize work, they must not break the journal's embargo and should coordinate timing/content with the journal press office to avoid premature release or conflicting messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of embargoes — fair access and reliance on peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nature Portfolio journals believe that their media embargo serves scientists, authors, journalists and the public by releasing information in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media, allowing it to provide informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes give journalists time to read the full peer-reviewed paper and obtain independent reactions; premature release denies journalists that confidence and removes their ability to obtain informed reactions from independent researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for journalists who break embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list, and we shall continue to use this sanction when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breach of embargo can lead to removal from future press-release access and other sanctions at the journal's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and conference presentations do not constitute prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals do not wish to hinder communication among researchers. Neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers may display drafts on established preprint servers before or during submission to Nature journals; posting preprints does not preempt submission or necessarily affect editorial handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media interactions regarding preprints or conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation, by providing explanation or clarification of the work, or information about its context. In these circumstances, media coverage will not hinder editorial handling of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When speaking to reporters about preprints/presentations, researchers should make clear the paper has not yet undergone peer review, that the findings are provisional and conclusions may change; researchers are expected to keep details of the peer review and editorial process confidential. Note that such coverage may reduce or pre-empt later media attention at time of formal publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to reporters covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: We also recommend that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should explicitly state preprint status and provisional nature of findings to avoid misleading audiences.
